Changes: Important: MSOP Configurator v1.1.0, or MESH v1.0.0 and newer, is required to download and install new versions of MSOP released after 30 September 2026 (2026.09.30). Please update to keep receiving MSOP updates.

General: This is the final release of the MSOP Configurator, which is being replaced by MESH (Modern Emulator State Hub). Once MESH is released, the MSOP Configurator will offer the upgrade every time it starts: it downloads MESH into the same folder and opens it, and MESH then removes the MSOP Configurator and its settings and walks you through a fresh setup. Your MAME installs and the MSOP Plugin are left as they are. The MSOP project itself (the MSOP Plugin for MAME) continues, and will be distributed via MESH moving forward. MESH GitHub: https://github.com/djGLiTCH/MESH

Compatibility: The MSOP Configurator supports MAME 0.200 to 0.288. MAME 0.289 removed the ability for plugins to register custom state outputs, so MAME 0.289 and newer need MESH, which supports MAME 0.200 and newer. Any MAME instance detected as version 0.289 or newer is now marked 'Requires MESH' and is skipped when installing or updating the MSOP Plugin.

Architectural Overhaul: All online content locations (MSOP Plugin, changelog, games database, Hooker Program files, and the Configurator's own updates) are now resolved from a single content manifest hosted on GitHub, so files can be reorganised in the repository in the future without breaking this final release.

General: Please note that MSOP Configurator v1.0.6 and MSOP Plugin v8.4.0 and all versions of these below are only compatible with MAME 0.200 to MAME 0.288 (unless MAME PR 15639 is applied to a custom MAME build). The upcoming official MAME 0.289+ release requires a new version of MSOP to work, as there is a fundamental change being implemented by the MAME devs that will prevent custom state outputs from being registered with MAME moving forward (and no code that enables this function will be allowed back into MAME). A new version of MSOP will be released in the near future that works around this limitation without the need for a custom MAME fork or build, and a working prototype is already undergoing testing.

init.lua: Reworked the relay retry policy from ongoing paced retries to a strictly bounded sequence, to stop the freezes reported on machines where security software silently drops loopback connection attempts (each failed connect blocks MAME for about 2 seconds, and the old schedule kept dialling for the whole session). Cold start (MESH never answered): one silent attempt at ROM start, one silent retry 10 seconds later, then an announced final attempt 30 seconds after that - and no further dialling for the session. Lost connection (MESH disconnected mid-game): one announced reconnect attempt 30 seconds after the drop, then no further dialling. Reconnecting afterwards costs one deliberate action: pause and unpause the game, soft reset, load a new ROM, or restart MAME - dialling never happens while paused, so recovery runs at the moment of unpause.

init.lua: Added clear on-screen (OSD) connection status messages, each shown at most once per session: 'MESH IS NOT RUNNING' (announcing the final cold attempt), 'MESH NOT FOUND - STATE OUTPUTS PAUSED' (cold attempts exhausted, with recovery steps), 'MESH DISCONNECTED' (the moment a live connection drops), 'MESH RECONNECT FAILED - STATE OUTPUTS PAUSED', and a 'MESH CONNECTED' confirmation once delivery is restored after any problem was reported. The OSD half is controlled by a new ENABLE_OSD_CONNECTION_STATUS flag in the database's _default block (enabled by default; absent = enabled) so genuine connection problems stay separate from the debug-gated diagnostics messages; the matching console messages always print regardless.

The notice recommends '-output none', the setup where MESH can serve external hooker programs the complete stream.

init.lua: '-output auto' (MAME's factory default) is now treated as 'none', which is exactly how MAME itself resolves it - verified in the source of MAME 0.200, 0.286, and current master alike. init.lua: Removed the adaptive dial-cost machinery (the 60-second escalating cap and per-dial timing) and the supported-versus-pass-through retry distinction - the bounded sequence makes both redundant, and every game now follows the same schedule.

init.lua: Optimised the per-frame paths. init.lua: Live native-output enumeration now works on stock MAME 0.290+, the first official release to carry the feature MSOP proposed upstream (mamedev/mame PR #15745). It landed in MAME in a different, more efficient form than the original proposal: 'device.outputs' is a container of live output proxies keyed by name, rather than a plain list of name pairs. MSOP's discovery was written against the proposal's shape and would have silently fallen back to the shipped lookup files; it now targets the accepted upstream form exclusively, and the live proxies are kept from discovery so per-output resolution is never repeated later. Note that official MAME 0.289 does not include the property - on 0.289 and earlier, native-output discovery continues to use the shipped lookup files.

init.lua: Each enumerated output's wire name is reconstructed exactly as MAME's own output modules format it (root-device outputs are unqualified; otherwise the owning device's tag, minus its leading colon, then ':', then the name) - so hooker payloads stay byte-identical to MAME's own broadcasts.

init.lua: The relay now dials MESH's dedicated MSOP ingest listener on 127.0.0.1:8004 (previously 8000). Port 8000 is the port MAME's own '-output network' server binds and every hooker program hard-codes, so sharing it meant a mixed fleet (an older MAME broadcasting natively beside a relay-path instance) fought over one port and whichever bound first silently won. The ingest port is private to MSOP and MESH - the plugin now never binds or dials port 8000 in any mode. An explicit 'relayport' value in plugin.json still wins over the default, exactly as before.

init.lua: Removed the '-output network' port derivation (the old step-aside to 8001). It existed only because the relay used to share MAME's port 8000; the dedicated ingest port cannot collide with MAME's server, so there is nothing to step aside from. The relay on/off decision itself is unchanged: capability first, then MAME version, then output mode - and with '-output network' or '-output windows' on MAME 0.288 or earlier, MSOP still opens no socket at all.

init.lua: Native-output pass-through for unsupported games now stands down based on MAME's resolved '-output' mode (network = MAME is already broadcasting those natives on 8000) rather than on the relay port - the previous port-based test would have wrongly disabled pass-through everywhere once the relay moved to its own port.

readme.txt: Documented the port split - the relay dials the MESH ingest port (default 8004, overridable via plugin.json's 'relayport'), while port 8000 remains MAME's own network output server and the hooker-facing side that MESH manages.

init.lua: Fixed the relay wrongly switching on for MAME 0.288 and earlier set to '-output network'. The derived relay port (8001, chosen to stay clear of MAME's own network server on 8000) was feeding a rule that treated any non-8000 port as a deliberate side-by-side arrangement and enabled the relay before the real decision gates ran - so a build that was already broadcasting everything itself also dialled 8001, producing pointless connection attempts, a misleading 'MESH is not running' warning, and (with a listener present) every MSOP output delivered twice. The port now only says where the relay lives; whether it runs is decided solely by the capability, version, and output-mode gates, which already force the relay on wherever it is genuinely required.

init.lua: With '-output network' or '-output windows' on MAME 0.288 and earlier, MSOP now opens no socket at all, as originally intended - MAME creates and broadcasts every output itself, MSOP's included, and MESH (or any hooker) reads that stream directly from MAME.

init.lua: Fixed a listener whose first relay connection happens at game exit never learning which ROM the session was. The 'mame_stop' broadcast can open the relay connection just-in-time, but the stored game announcement was cleared before that broadcast - so the new listener received the dying game's final values and 'mame_stop' with no 'mame_start', an unidentifiable session. The stop notice is now sent while the announcement still holds the running game (so a just-in-time connection receives the correct 'mame_start -> final values -> mame_stop' sequence), and the announcement is cleared afterwards - preserving the guarantee that a connection made after the game has ended never re-announces a stale ROM.
init.lua: On (re)connect, the full state resync is now skipped when no game is announced - with no session identity on the wire, a fresh listener could not attribute the replayed values to any ROM.

init.lua: The 'nothing is listening on the relay' warning now names MESH directly and appears promptly. init.lua: Fixed a listener that connects mid-game not learning which ROM is running. Previously the output values were replayed on reconnect but the game announcement was not, so a slightly-late listener saw the outputs yet never learned the game. init.lua: Added resilience for when nothing is listening on the relay. Reconnect attempts are now adaptive to how expensive a failed connection is on the machine: where local firewall or security software silently drops loopback connection attempts (making each failed dial cost a couple of seconds rather than failing instantly), the never-answered retry interval backs off further - up to 60 seconds - so a missing listener no longer holds emulation at reduced speed for the whole session.

init.lua: For an unsupported (pass-through) game, MSOP now stops dialling the relay after a few failed attempts when nothing has ever answered, since such a game carries only mirrored native outputs and is not worth stalling emulation for. It re-arms automatically on the next ROM start, soft reset, or unpause, so starting MESH later still connects.

init.lua: Added a one-time on-screen (OSD) and console warning the first time a session concludes that nothing is listening on the relay, so the absence of force feedback is explained rather than mysterious.

init.lua: Simplified the output-creation capability check to the single route that still exists on an official build (the deprecated set_value probe, tested for real), removing the obsolete 'register_output' detection that never applies to a stock MAME.

init.lua: The relay is now enabled from capability rather than from the MAME version string. Custom and pre-release builds can report a version that does not match their behaviour, and guessing from the number alone left '-output windows' silently undelivered.

init.lua: The relay port is now derived from MAME's own '-output' setting, with nothing to configure. An explicit 'relayport' value in plugin.json still wins.

init.lua: Added optional pass-through of a game driver's own native state outputs over the relay, for ROMs MSOP has no profile for. Requires the new optional database_mame_driver.lua lookup (see below) and applies only with '-output none' or '-output console'; with '-output network' MAME already broadcasts those itself.

init.lua: Reworked relay reconnect pacing. Retries were counted in frames, which is not a wall-clock cadence at all - roughly one attempt per second at normal speed and far more with throttling off. That matters because a refused connection is not always cheap: where local firewall or security software silently drops loopback connection attempts rather than refusing them, the operating system waits out its retransmit first, measured at about 2 seconds, and MAME's socket open is a plain blocking call with no timeout setting. With nothing listening on the relay port this held MAME at roughly 45% of full speed. Retries are now timed on a real monotonic clock and backed off: one free attempt at every ROM start where the pause hides inside loading, then 2s / 4s / 8s / 15s after losing a relay that was there, or 5s / 10s / 15s when nothing has ever answered, capped at 15 seconds. Measured on Point Blank 2 with nothing listening, this restored 44% to 377% of full speed, against 429% with a relay present. Retries never stop, so starting the MESH app after MAME still connects on its own.

database_mame_driver.lua: New optional database of the native output names MAME's own game drivers create (lamp0, Player1_Gun_Recoil, P1_Start_lamp and so on), keyed by driver source file so a single entry covers every ROM that driver builds. Place it in the stateoutput folder beside database.lua to have MSOP carry both its own outputs and the game's native ones over one connection to 127.0.0.1:8000, including for games MSOP does not support. Without the file nothing breaks and unsupported games simply produce nothing, as before. Measured cost with the file present was within about 1% of running without it.
readme.txt: Documented the two-port arrangement, the version rule of thumb for official builds, the optional database_mame_driver.lua file, and the reconnect back-off.

init.lua: Added pass-through mode for games MSOP has no profile for. init.lua: Added a new derived P*_Clip output - 1 while a player still has ammo, 0 the moment the clip empties (a reload is needed). It is published only for games with a genuinely depleting ammo clip (AMMO_DIRECTION 'decrease'), because that is the only reading where 0 unambiguously means empty; a game whose ammo counts up (a shots-fired counter) or can swap weapons with an unknown capacity does not expose it, rather than risk publishing an inverted reload signal. Being derived from ammo rather than read from a memory address, it needs no database rebuild to appear.

Note: MSOP Plugin v9.0.0+ works with official MAME 0.289 and later, with no custom fork or patched build required. MAME 0.289 removed the ability for a Lua plugin to create state outputs, so MAME can no longer hold - and therefore no longer broadcast - any of MSOP's outputs. From v9.0.0 those outputs are delivered over MSOP's own relay (a loopback TCP connection provided by the MSOP Configurator / MESH) instead. MAME 0.200 to 0.288 are unaffected and continue to deliver natively.

init.lua: Introduced the relay delivery path. When the running MAME build cannot broadcast MSOP's outputs (MAME 0.289+, or '-output none'/'console'), MSOP connects to the relay as a TCP client and streams its state outputs there instead of relying on MAME's own output modules; on older builds that still deliver natively the relay stays off. The relay decision is resolved at runtime from MAME's version and '-output' mode, with a per-install fallback flag stamped into plugin.json by the MSOP Configurator / MESH.

init.lua: On every relay (re)connect MSOP resends the full current value of every output, so a listener that starts - or restarts - after the game is already running immediately receives the complete state rather than only the values that happen to change afterwards.

init.lua: Added a new 'always' value for the game profile GAME_STATUS field. A game with no known game-state memory address can now declare the game active whenever it is running - after warmup, and still respecting an address-backed ATTRACT_STATUS where one is configured. Without it, a profile with no per-player activity signals could never raise the MSOP_GameStatus output, leaving status-gated consumers dark and the derived attract flag stuck on for the whole session. init.lua: Reworked the relay retry policy from ongoing paced retries to a strictly bounded sequence, to stop the freezes reported on machines where security software silently drops loopback connection attempts (each failed connect blocks MAME for about 2 seconds, and the old schedule kept dialling for the whole session). Cold start (MESH never answered): one silent attempt at ROM start, one silent retry 10 seconds later, then an announced final attempt 30 seconds after that - and no further dialling for the session. Lost connection (MESH disconnected mid-game): one announced reconnect attempt 30 seconds after the drop, then no further dialling. Reconnecting afterwards costs one deliberate action: pause and unpause the game, soft reset, load a new ROM, or restart MAME - dialling never happens while paused, so recovery runs at the moment of unpause.

init.lua: Added clear on-screen (OSD) connection status messages, each shown at most once per session: 'MESH IS NOT RUNNING' (announcing the final cold attempt), 'MESH NOT FOUND - STATE OUTPUTS PAUSED' (cold attempts exhausted, with recovery steps), 'MESH DISCONNECTED' (the moment a live connection drops), 'MESH RECONNECT FAILED - STATE OUTPUTS PAUSED', and a 'MESH CONNECTED' confirmation once delivery is restored after any problem was reported. The OSD half is controlled by a new ENABLE_OSD_CONNECTION_STATUS flag in the database's _default block (enabled by default; absent = enabled) so genuine connection problems stay separate from the debug-gated diagnostics messages; the matching console messages always print regardless.

init.lua: Added an 'INCORRECT OUTPUT MODE DETECTED' notice for MAME builds that cannot create MSOP's outputs (0.289 and above) running with '-output network' or '-output windows' - modes that only deliver MSOP's outputs natively on MAME 0.200 - 0.288. The notice recommends '-output none', the setup where MESH can serve external hooker programs the complete stream.

init.lua: '-output auto' (MAME's factory default) is now treated as 'none', which is exactly how MAME itself resolves it - verified in the source of MAME 0.200, 0.286, and current master alike. Previously 'auto' fell through to the per-install stamp fallback, which a hand-installed plugin does not have, leaving a default-configured MAME 0.288 or earlier silently undelivered.

init.lua: Removed the adaptive dial-cost machinery (the 60-second escalating cap and per-dial timing) and the supported-versus-pass-through retry distinction - the bounded sequence makes both redundant, and every game now follows the same schedule.
database: _default.json gains ENABLE_OSD_CONNECTION_STATUS (default true) - set it to false to silence the connection status OSD messages while keeping the console messages.

readme.txt: Rewrote the 'IF NOTHING IS LISTENING ON THE RELAY PORT' section for the bounded retry policy, the new status messages and their toggle, the incorrect output mode notice, and the '-output auto' behaviour.

init.lua: Optimised the per-frame paths. For racing games, the force feedback decoder and scale are now resolved once per ROM load instead of every frame, and the decoder only runs when the raw command value actually changes (identical values decode to identical outputs, which were already deduplicated). Native-output proxy resolution no longer allocates a closure per attempt.

init.lua: Live native-output enumeration now works on stock MAME 0.290+, the first official release to carry the feature MSOP proposed upstream (mamedev/mame PR #15745). It landed in MAME in a different, more efficient form than the original proposal: 'device.outputs' is a container of live output proxies keyed by name, rather than a plain list of name pairs. MSOP's discovery was written against the proposal's shape and would have silently fallen back to the shipped lookup files; it now targets the accepted upstream form exclusively, and the live proxies are kept from discovery so per-output resolution is never repeated later. Note that official MAME 0.289 does not include the property - on 0.289 and earlier, native-output discovery continues to use the shipped lookup files.

init.lua: Each enumerated output's wire name is reconstructed exactly as MAME's own output modules format it (root-device outputs are unqualified; otherwise the owning device's tag, minus its leading colon, then ':', then the name) - so hooker payloads stay byte-identical to MAME's own broadcasts.

readme.txt: Updated the native-output discovery section - live enumeration becomes the stock behaviour on MAME 0.290 and later, with the shipped lookup files serving MAME 0.289 and earlier (official 0.289 does not provide 'device.outputs').

Note: MSOP Plugin v9.3.0 pairs with the port-split MESH release. MESH's health check will flag relay-path instances running an older plugin once the split ships. MESH-managed installs self-correct on their next plugin update in either order, because MESH stamps the relay port explicitly into plugin.json and the plugin honours that stamp.

init.lua: The relay now dials MESH's dedicated MSOP ingest listener on 127.0.0.1:8004 (previously 8000). Port 8000 is the port MAME's own '-output network' server binds and every hooker program hard-codes, so sharing it meant a mixed fleet (an older MAME broadcasting natively beside a relay-path instance) fought over one port and whichever bound first silently won. The ingest port is private to MSOP and MESH - the plugin now never binds or dials port 8000 in any mode. An explicit 'relayport' value in plugin.json still wins over the default, exactly as before.

init.lua: Removed the '-output network' port derivation (the old step-aside to 8001). It existed only because the relay used to share MAME's port 8000; the dedicated ingest port cannot collide with MAME's server, so there is nothing to step aside from. The relay on/off decision itself is unchanged: capability first, then MAME version, then output mode - and with '-output network' or '-output windows' on MAME 0.288 or earlier, MSOP still opens no socket at all.

init.lua: Native-output pass-through for unsupported games now stands down based on MAME's resolved '-output' mode (network = MAME is already broadcasting those natives on 8000) rather than on the relay port - the previous port-based test would have wrongly disabled pass-through everywhere once the relay moved to its own port.

readme.txt: Documented the port split - the relay dials the MESH ingest port (default 8004, overridable via plugin.json's 'relayport'), while port 8000 remains MAME's own network output server and the hooker-facing side that MESH manages.

init.lua: Fixed the relay wrongly switching on for MAME 0.288 and earlier set to '-output network'. The derived relay port (8001, chosen to stay clear of MAME's own network server on 8000) was feeding a rule that treated any non-8000 port as a deliberate side-by-side arrangement and enabled the relay before the real decision gates ran - so a build that was already broadcasting everything itself also dialled 8001, producing pointless connection attempts, a misleading 'MESH is not running' warning, and (with a listener present) every MSOP output delivered twice. The port now only says where the relay lives; whether it runs is decided solely by the capability, version, and output-mode gates, which already force the relay on wherever it is genuinely required.

init.lua: With '-output network' or '-output windows' on MAME 0.288 and earlier, MSOP now opens no socket at all, as originally intended - MAME creates and broadcasts every output itself, MSOP's included, and MESH (or any hooker) reads that stream directly from MAME.

init.lua: Fixed a listener whose first relay connection happens at game exit never learning which ROM the session was. The 'mame_stop' broadcast can open the relay connection just-in-time, but the stored game announcement was cleared before that broadcast - so the new listener received the dying game's final values and 'mame_stop' with no 'mame_start', an unidentifiable session. The stop notice is now sent while the announcement still holds the running game (so a just-in-time connection receives the correct 'mame_start -> final values -> mame_stop' sequence), and the announcement is cleared afterwards - preserving the guarantee that a connection made after the game has ended never re-announces a stale ROM.
init.lua: On (re)connect, the full state resync is now skipped when no game is announced - with no session identity on the wire, a fresh listener could not attribute the replayed values to any ROM.
init.lua: Tidied the code documentation throughout and removed version-specific references from comments.

init.lua: Added a new GAME_TYPE field to the game database ('lightgun', 'racing', or 'both'; per game, with a database-wide default). 'lightgun' - the default, and the behaviour of every existing profile - runs the classic per-player gun pipeline and compiles the gun output vocabulary. 'racing' skips the per-player gun pipeline entirely and compiles only the FFB_ force feedback vocabulary. 'both' does it all, for hybrid games. Unknown values degrade to 'lightgun', so existing game profiles are untouched by the new field.
init.lua: Added the FFB_ force feedback output vocabulary for racing-genre games, decoded from each game's own native MAME outputs.
database: Added racing game support covering the games the FFB Arcade Plugin project drives through a decodable MAME output.

init.lua: Made it obvious - in both MAME's console and the on-screen display (OSD) - that MESH must be running whenever the relay is the delivery path. When the relay is in use (MAME 0.289+, or '-output none'/'console'), MSOP now prints an up-front console banner stating that MSOP is sending its state outputs to the relay and MESH must be running to receive and forward them. Previously this was only in the debug log, which most users never see, so a missing MESH looked like a fault with no explanation.

init.lua: The 'nothing is listening on the relay' warning now names MESH directly and appears promptly. For a supported game it is shown after about 5 seconds (one retry of grace for a MESH that is still starting) instead of only after the full retry schedule (~30 seconds), so a player whose force feedback is silent is told the reason - MESH is not running - almost immediately, on both the console and the OSD. The successful-connection message likewise now confirms MESH is receiving MSOP's outputs.

init.lua: Fixed a listener that connects mid-game not learning which ROM is running. The running game's 'mame_start' announcement is now stored and re-sent on every relay (re)connect, so MESH (or a hooker) that attaches a moment after the ROM has started still receives the game name and loads the correct profile. Previously the output values were replayed on reconnect but the game announcement was not, so a slightly-late listener saw the outputs yet never learned the game. The mame_stop and pause notices remain deliberately one-shot.

init.lua: Added resilience for when nothing is listening on the relay. Reconnect attempts are now adaptive to how expensive a failed connection is on the machine: where local firewall or security software silently drops loopback connection attempts (making each failed dial cost a couple of seconds rather than failing instantly), the never-answered retry interval backs off further - up to 60 seconds - so a missing listener no longer holds emulation at reduced speed for the whole session.

init.lua: For an unsupported (pass-through) game, MSOP now stops dialling the relay after a few failed attempts when nothing has ever answered, since such a game carries only mirrored native outputs and is not worth stalling emulation for. It re-arms automatically on the next ROM start, soft reset, or unpause, so starting MESH later still connects.

init.lua: Added a one-time on-screen (OSD) and console warning the first time a session concludes that nothing is listening on the relay, so the absence of force feedback is explained rather than mysterious.

init.lua: Added live enumeration of a game's own native MAME outputs via MAME's read-only 'device.outputs' property. For a game MSOP has no profile for, this forwards that game's real native outputs over the relay whether or not its driver was ever scraped into a lookup file - exact coverage, and preferred over the scraped-file fallback when the running build supports it.

native_outputs_by_rom.lua / native_outputs_by_driver.lua: Renamed the optional scraped native-output databases so their names describe their contents - 'database_driver.lua' is now 'native_outputs_by_rom.lua' (ROM-keyed) and 'database_mame_driver.lua' is now 'native_outputs_by_driver.lua' (driver-source-keyed, one entry covering every ROM a driver builds).

init.lua: Simplified the output-creation capability check to the single route that still exists on an official build (the deprecated set_value probe, tested for real), removing the obsolete 'register_output' detection that never applies to a stock MAME.

init.lua: The relay is now enabled from capability rather than from the MAME version string. MSOP asks the running build whether it can create a custom output, by both the modern route (register_output) and the deprecated one (output.set_value, tested for real), and switches the relay on only when neither works. Custom and pre-release builds can report a version that does not match their behaviour, and guessing from the number alone left '-output windows' silently undelivered.

init.lua: The relay port is now derived from MAME's own '-output' setting, with nothing to configure. MAME's network output server binds a hard-coded port 8000, so MSOP uses 8001 with '-output network' and 8000 with none, console or windows - 8000 being where every hooker program looks. An explicit 'relayport' value in plugin.json still wins.

init.lua: Added optional pass-through of a game driver's own native state outputs over the relay, for ROMs MSOP has no profile for. Requires the new optional database_mame_driver.lua lookup (see below) and applies only with '-output none' or '-output console'; with '-output network' MAME already broadcasts those itself.

init.lua: Reworked relay reconnect pacing. Retries were counted in frames, which is not a wall-clock cadence at all - roughly one attempt per second at normal speed and far more with throttling off. That matters because a refused connection is not always cheap: where local firewall or security software silently drops loopback connection attempts rather than refusing them, the operating system waits out its retransmit first, measured at about 2 seconds, and MAME's socket open is a plain blocking call with no timeout setting. With nothing listening on the relay port this held MAME at roughly 45% of full speed. Retries are now timed on a real monotonic clock and backed off: one free attempt at every ROM start where the pause hides inside loading, then 2s / 4s / 8s / 15s after losing a relay that was there, or 5s / 10s / 15s when nothing has ever answered, capped at 15 seconds. Measured on Point Blank 2 with nothing listening, this restored 44% to 377% of full speed, against 429% with a relay present. Retries never stop, so starting the MESH app after MAME still connects on its own.

database_mame_driver.lua: New optional database of the native output names MAME's own game drivers create (lamp0, Player1_Gun_Recoil, P1_Start_lamp and so on), keyed by driver source file so a single entry covers every ROM that driver builds. Place it in the stateoutput folder beside database.lua to have MSOP carry both its own outputs and the game's native ones over one connection to 127.0.0.1:8000, including for games MSOP does not support. Without the file nothing breaks and unsupported games simply produce nothing, as before. Measured cost with the file present was within about 1% of running without it.
readme.txt: Documented the two-port arrangement, the version rule of thumb for official builds, the optional database_mame_driver.lua file, and the reconnect back-off.

init.lua: Added pass-through mode for games MSOP has no profile for. Under the relay (with '-output none'/'console') MAME's own network output server never runs, so an unsupported game's native lamps/LEDs/etc. would otherwise reach nothing; MSOP now mirrors that game's known native outputs (from the optional scraped database_driver.lua) over the relay so an unsupported game still delivers them. A ROM with no scraped entry simply forwards nothing, as before.

init.lua: Fixed an unsupported game neither forwarding anything nor flushing the relay at all - the frame handler now runs for pass-through games instead of returning early whenever there was no MSOP profile.

init.lua: Added a new derived P*_Clip output - 1 while a player still has ammo, 0 the moment the clip empties (a reload is needed). It is published only for games with a genuinely depleting ammo clip (AMMO_DIRECTION 'decrease'), because that is the only reading where 0 unambiguously means empty; a game whose ammo counts up (a shots-fired counter) or can swap weapons with an unknown capacity does not expose it, rather than risk publishing an inverted reload signal. Being derived from ammo rather than read from a memory address, it needs no database rebuild to appear.

Note: MSOP Plugin v9.0.0+ works with official MAME 0.289 and later, with no custom fork or patched build required. MAME 0.289 removed the ability for a Lua plugin to create state outputs, so MAME can no longer hold - and therefore no longer broadcast - any of MSOP's outputs. From v9.0.0 those outputs are delivered over MSOP's own relay (a loopback TCP connection provided by the MSOP Configurator / MESH) instead. MAME 0.200 to 0.288 are unaffected and continue to deliver natively.

init.lua: Introduced the relay delivery path. When the running MAME build cannot broadcast MSOP's outputs (MAME 0.289+, or '-output none'/'console'), MSOP connects to the relay as a TCP client and streams its state outputs there instead of relying on MAME's own output modules; on older builds that still deliver natively the relay stays off. The relay decision is resolved at runtime from MAME's version and '-output' mode, with a per-install fallback flag stamped into plugin.json by the MSOP Configurator / MESH.

init.lua: On every relay (re)connect MSOP resends the full current value of every output, so a listener that starts - or restarts - after the game is already running immediately receives the complete state rather than only the values that happen to change afterwards.
readme.txt: Documented the relay-based delivery model and MAME 0.289+ compatibility.

Note: As of 2026.07.03, MAME PR 15639 (https://github.com/mamedev/mame/pull/15639) has been rejected, and so MSOP Plugin v8.4.0 and below are only compatible with MAME 0.200 to 0.288 unless MAME PR 15639 is applied to a custom MAME 0.289+ build. A future MSOP update will be released shortly that will work without a custom MAME build, and is expected in MSOP Configurator v2.0.0+ and MSOP Plugin v9.0.0+ (both will be required moving forward, not just MSOP Plugin).

init.lua: Reworked logic so that MSOP Plugin complies with the requirements of MAME 0.289+ if PR #15639 is applied. Removed the logic that was added in MSOP Plugin v8.3.0 since that applied to PR #15618 instead. Fallback logic that existed previously is still in place for official releases of MAME 0.200 to 0.288.
readme.txt: Expanded 'Output Mappings' section so it is clear what state outputs need to be mapped to commands in MAMEhooker, OutputHooker, and/or QMamehook.

Note: As of 2026.07.01, MAME PR 15618 (https://github.com/mamedev/mame/pull/15618) has been rejected, and so a new pull request will be created with a different solution proposal to this problem. MSOP Plugin v8.3.0 at this time will be compatible with MAME 0.288 and below, or with MAME 0.289 and MAME PR 15618 applied to a custom MAME build.

init.lua: Implement 'Safe Setter' architecture. Centralises output management by abstracting Set_Output_Safe and Get_Output_Proxy, ensuring seamless compatibility between modern device-scoped MAME (0.289+) and legacy MAME releases.
init.lua: Implement 'Output Proxy Cache' function. Caches output_proxy objects at boot to eliminate redundant dictionary lookups and dynamic resolution overhead during the 60Hz frame loop.
init.lua: Encapsulate proxy resolution in pcall handlers. Prevents plugin crashes in environments lacking specific MAME API features, ensuring safe fallback to standard set_value operations.
readme.txt: Added 'Output Mappings' section so it is clear what state outputs need to be mapped to commands in MAMEhooker, OutputHooker, and/or QMamehook.

init.lua: Added new function RELOAD_MEM_MIN_VALUE so that if any number equal to or above this value is identified then this will trigger a reload (useful if games have multiple weapons that differ in ammo capacity, but you don't know the specific ammo available for each weapon).

init.lua: Expanded logic for GAME_STATUS_ACTIVE_VALUE so that an array can be used, which allows multiple values to be used (useful if the same memory address is shared between GAME_STATUS and ATTRACT_MODE_STATUS).
init.lua: Expanded logic for RELOAD_MEM_ADD_VALUE so that an array can be used, which allows multiple values to be used as triggers for reload (if they are known).
init.lua: Fixed logic used for ATTRACT_STATUS_ACTIVE_VALUE (this was incorrectly causing GAME_STATUS to override to 0 in some instances).
init.lua: Fixed code documentation so it reads more clearly to others.
init.lua: Removed accidental logic that in some cases would combine recoil and damage together.
readme.txt: Revised formatting and contents of readme file for MSOP Plugin.
init.lua: Added new feature to support enabling or disabling individual supported game ROMs with MSOP Plugin (in case MSOP causes clashes with custom scripts some users have for specific games).

init.lua: Added new feature that enables access to memory space as a 'region', which will hook directly into the physical ROM memory region instead of the CPU address space to allow safe patching (required in some instances for functions like Screen Flash removal).
init.lua: Added new feature that enables per player screen flash removal for games where each player can trigger a screen flash independently of each other.
init.lua: Added new feature that enables 64-bit data width for reading and writing memory address values.
init.lua: Fixed the PX_CreditsConsumed logic so that it correctly works for games where LIFE_DIRECTION = 'increase' (previously it was only working in games where LIFE_DIRECTION = 'decrease').

init.lua: Revised the PX_CreditsConsumed logic to account for instances where Player Status may change faster than the Credit counter can decrease. This will need to be checked against each game to check for logic edge cases.
init.lua: Fixed Damage and DamageTaken from triggering in certain edge cases when a player's life increases despite logic dictacting that an increase in life does not relate to a damage state event.

init.lua: Fixed flushing of warmup values when opening consecutive ROMs without fully exiting MAME between each ROM launch. This will ensure force feedback is disabled until a player is active in the game.
init.lua: Fixed ShotsFired and ShotsFiredPrimary so that in games where ammo may equal 0 but shots can still be fired at half rate, the counters will still continue to increase as appropriate.

ChangesDatabaseCompiler: msop_database_compiler.py: Game JSONs may now be organised into subfolders under database/games/ (e.g. games/lightgun/ and games/racing/). Mode 1 ingests the games tree recursively - the folder a file sits in is organisational only, the ROM key is always the file name, and the same ROM appearing in two places is a build error (reported with both locations, and the build exits non-zero).

msop_database_compiler.py: Mode 2 (splitting database.json back into per-game files) now sorts each game into its game-type subfolder - games/lightgun/, games/racing/, or games/both/ per the game's GAME_TYPE, with missing or unknown values placed in lightgun/ exactly as the plugin resolves them. _default.json stays at the games/ root, and any stale copy of a ROM at a different location is removed and reported as moved, so the same ROM can never exist twice.

msop_output_model.py: The shared output model (used by the HOTR defaultLG and MAMEhooker INI generators) now discovers game files recursively, so both generators work unchanged with game-type subfolders.
msop_native_outputs_compiler.py: The supported-games list is now gathered recursively for the same reason.

msop_database_compiler.py: The metadata sync now also strips a stray 'relayport' member from plugin.json, alongside the existing 'relay' strip. Both are deploy-time stamps the MESH app writes into installed copies; the shipped plugin must stay pristine so a manual install self-detects its relay mode and uses the default relay port.

msop_database_compiler.py: Fixed a fatal startup error introduced in 3.4.1 - print_banner referenced an undefined 'date_str' variable, so every run aborted with a NameError before compiling anything. Anyone on 3.4.1 must update to 3.4.2 for the compiler to run at all.

msop_database_compiler.py: The compiled database date is no longer attempted in the startup banner (it is not resolved until part-way through a run); it continues to be reported as 'Database Date' in the end-of-run summary.

Per-channel builds: input/ and output/ are now split into stable/ and beta/ trees, each holding its own stateoutput/ plugin source and database/games/ folder, so a beta database (new or untested games, or an experimental init.lua) can never contaminate the stable build.

msop_database_compiler.py: Added --channel stable|beta so the compiler reads and writes only that channel's tree; the existing headless stable/beta argument now selects the tree as well as stamping plugin.json.
msop_database_driver_compiler.py: Added --channel stable|beta, with the games, output and scrape-report paths all defaulting to that channel's tree.

msop_hotr_defaultlg_generator.py: New generator that builds a Hook Of The Reaper defaultLG mapping file for every supported game directly from the database - recoil and reload are always driven by the dedicated MSOP commands, and ammo is used for display only.
msop_mamehooker_ini_generator.py: New generator that builds a blank MAMEhooker-style .ini for every supported game, with its [Output] section prepopulated with exactly the outputs that game emits.

msop_mamehooker_ini_generator.py: The .ini skeletons are MSOP-only by default (the plugin's own state outputs plus each game's curated ADDITIONAL_OUTPUT_FORWARDS); pass --include-driver to also fold in the MAME native outputs scraped into database_driver.lua.
msop_output_model.py: New shared helper library holding the authoritative per-game output derivation (mirroring init.lua's own emission rules), so both generators always resolve the same output set.

Launchers: run_stable.* and run_beta.* now run the full per-channel pipeline (database compile, optional driver compile, HOTR templates, then MAMEhooker INIs), and run.* builds both channels in one pass.
Launchers: Added run_stable_msop_only.* and run_beta_msop_only.* to build a driver-free channel (no database_driver.lua, MSOP-only INIs), plus single-purpose launchers for each template generator.
Launchers: Added run_msop_database_driver_compiler.* to run only the MAME native-output scrape and refresh database_driver.lua without rebuilding anything else.
duckhunt.json: MAX_PLAYERS set to 1 so this single-player-only game no longer generates Player 2 outputs or templates.
msop_database_compiler.py: Fixed script for updating readme.txt version and date to locate the correct readme.txt file in the OUTPUT_DIR (stateoutput) folder.
msop_database_compiler.py: Added error detection support for duplicate fields within JSON game profiles.
readme.txt: Created new readme file to explain how to use the MSOP Compiler and configure support for new games.
